title: Hours Back: AI for the Small Office
tagline: Use AI to give your team its evenings back, with nobody replaced and you approving everything.
audience: Owners and office managers of businesses with 2 to 20 people
Bookkeepers and admin staff who chase quotes, invoices and documents
Anyone who wants a calm, practical start with no jargon
outcomes: Measure where your office hours go, using your own numbers
Choose one repeat job to hand over and score it honestly
Write an approval rule so a person checks every message
Draft inbox, chasing, notes, roster and onboarding messages you review before sending
Know what never to paste into an AI tool and where to ask for professional advice
Prove a before and after result for your own office

questions.q: What is the first thing to do before changing any admin routine?
options: Buy an AI tool
Log where your hours actually go for a week
Ask the team to work faster
Set up automatic sending
questions.why: You measure first. Your own log shows which jobs really take the time.

questions.q: Which job is a good first one to hand over?
options: Replying to a formal complaint
Deciding a staff disciplinary matter
A repeat job with a clear finish line, such as a quote follow-up
Giving tax advice to a client
questions.why: Repeat, wordy jobs with a clear finish and a low cost of error suit drafting. Sensitive matters need a person.

questions.q: What does the approval rule say?
options: AI drafts, and a named person reads and approves every message
AI sends routine messages on its own
Approval is only needed for new clients
The AI tool checks its own work
questions.why: A human approves every message, and the rule works best when a named person is responsible.

questions.q: A draft has an invoice amount in it. What should you do?
options: Trust it, the tool is good with numbers
Delete the amount
Send it and fix any complaint later
Check it against your accounting records
questions.why: Drafts can be wrong. Names, dates and amounts are checked against your own records.

questions.q: Which of these should never be pasted into an AI tool?
options: A friendly reminder template with square brackets
Tax file numbers and bank details
A made-up example with no real names
Your own list of questions
questions.why: Identity, bank and similar sensitive details do not go into outside tools.

questions.q: What is the best way to use AI on your inbox?
options: Forward everything to it and let it reply
Let it decide which clients matter
Stop reading the inbox yourself
Paste a few messages with private details removed and ask it to sort by urgency
questions.why: Use it to help you decide what to look at first, with details removed, and read the originals yourself.

questions.q: What should the AI do when it does not know a fact, according to a good prompt?
options: Make a sensible guess
Skip the sentence silently
Leave a clear gap in square brackets
Copy from an old message
questions.why: A blank you must fill is safer than an invented date or amount.

questions.q: What are the Australian Privacy Principles, at a plain level?
options: Rules about how personal information is collected, used, stored and disclosed
Rules only about advertising
Rules for AI tools only
Optional tips for large companies
questions.why: They are part of the Privacy Act. Whether and how they apply to you is a question for a lawyer or other professional.

questions.q: When you measure a saving, which time must you count?
options: Only the drafting time
Only the time the tool took
Instruction, reading, correcting and approving time as well
Only the time you remember
questions.why: A saving that ignores checking is not a saving.

questions.q: What if your after result is small or negative?
options: Hide it and try another tool
Claim the saving anyway
Stop using any measuring
Record it, change one thing such as the prompt, and measure again
questions.why: An honest small or negative result is still a result and tells you what to change.

questions.q: What is the aim of this course for your team?
options: To give people their hours back with nobody replaced
To replace admin staff
To let AI run the office
To collect your data
questions.why: The principle is that hours are given back, nobody is replaced, and people stay in charge.

questions.q: Who should answer a question about what is deductible or what your legal duties are?
options: The AI tool
A registered tax agent, accountant or lawyer
Whoever replies first online
The newest staff member
questions.why: AI can help you phrase the question, but advice on tax or law comes from a professional.
